content.content:
---
redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/ghostfolio/ghostfolio
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: ghostfolio/ghostfolio:3.53.0 (plus redis:alpine in the same compose)
  port: 3333
  vm: m1.medium
  flavor_id: "3"
  database: managed postgres (redu-managed, own private VM, m1.small via db_flavor_id "2")
  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0452
bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: ghostfolio
quirks:
  - "THIS IS A TWO-SERVICE STACK, SO deploy_compose, NEVER deploy_app. Start from docker/docker-compose.yml (NOT docker-compose.dev.yml and NOT docker-compose.build.yml, which builds the monorepo from source) and adapt it: keep the ghostfolio service and the redis service, DELETE the postgres service, and pull the pinned image. Nothing is built."
  - "⛔ PIN THE IMAGE. ghostfolio/ghostfolio:3.53.0 (Docker Hub, published 2026-08-16, digest sha256:«REDACTED:longhex:c6962cad»). Upstream's compose says :latest and this project ships roughly ONE RELEASE PER DAY: 3.42.0 through 3.53.0 all landed inside twelve days. A rolling tag here is not a small risk, it is a near-certainty that your next redeploy runs a different application than the one you verified."
  - "⛔⛔ WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR, AND WHEN: THE FIRST ACCOUNT CREATED BECOMES ADMIN, AND ACCOUNT CREATION IS ANONYMOUS AND OPEN ON A FRESH DATABASE. Verified in apps/api/src/app/user/user.service.ts:693-697, where role is ADMIN when no admin exists yet, and user.controller.ts:142-170, where POST /api/v1/user carries NO auth guard and is gated only on a Property row that does not exist yet. There is no install wizard, no env var for it and no default password. The window is open from the moment the hostname answers until somebody claims the account, so CLAIM IT AS PART OF THE DEPLOY, before you hand over the URL. Two steps, in this order: (1) POST /api/v1/user and check the response says role ADMIN, saving the accessToken it returns; (2) close signup with the next quirk. Never leave an unclaimed Ghostfolio on a public hostname."
  - "⛔ IS REGISTRATION OPEN AFTER THE FIRST ACCOUNT? YES, AND CLOSING IT IS A DATABASE ROW, NOT A SETTING YOU CAN SHIP. apps/api/src/services/property/property.service.ts:63-68 reads IS_USER_SIGNUP_ENABLED from the Property table and defaults to TRUE when the row is absent, and there is no environment variable that overrides it. The row is written by an authenticated admin through PUT /api/v1/admin/settings/IS_USER_SIGNUP_ENABLED with a JSON body of {\"value\":\"false\"} (apps/api/src/app/admin/admin.controller.ts:316-324); the value is a STRING that the service JSON.parses, so send the four characters false, not 0 and not a boolean. ⚠️ Properties are cached in memory for one minute, but putSetting invalidates that cache, so the change takes effect at once. VERIFY IT BY BEHAVIOUR, NOT BY THE FLAG: an anonymous POST /api/v1/user must answer 403. Reading createUserAccount out of /api/v1/info is a useful cross-check and is NOT the proof."
  - "⛔ THE RATE LIMIT ON SIGNUP AND ON LOGIN IS OFF BY DEFAULT, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT THE CODE LOOKS LIKE. The signup route carries a Throttle of 5 per hour and the token-login route carries the default 10 per minute, but apps/api/src/app/app.module.ts:157-185 configures the throttler with skipIf returning true whenever ENABLE_FEATURE_RATE_LIMITING is false, and configuration.service.ts:76 defaults it to FALSE. So out of the box those decorators do nothing at all. SET ENABLE_FEATURE_RATE_LIMITING=true, and set TRUST_PROXY=1 alongside it: main.ts:123-129 warns that without it every client behind redu's proxy shares one bucket, which turns a rate limit into a self-inflicted outage. With it enabled the throttler stores its counters in the Redis you already have."
  - "⛔⛔ ACCESS_TOKEN_SALT IS THE SECRET THAT A REDEPLOY DESTROYS, AND HERE IT IS UNRECOVERABLE. Ghostfolio's default login has no e-mail and no password: «REDACTED:assigned:c5683ead» hands the user a long random token once, and stores that token hashed AGAIN with ACCESS_TOKEN_SALT. auth.service.ts:19-36 logs in by recomputing that hash with the same salt and looking the user up by it. Change the salt and every stored hash stops matching, so EVERY user including the admin is locked out permanently, with all the portfolio data still sitting in Postgres and no reset flow to get back in. Generate it once, record it with the user, and pass the identical value on every redeploy. JWT_SECRET_KEY is the milder sibling: changing it only invalidates live sessions. Both are declared without a default (configuration.service.ts:47,86), so a MISSING one exits the process at boot, which is the good case; a CHANGED one is silent."
  - "TELL THE USER, IN WORDS, THAT THE SECURITY TOKEN IS SHOWN ONCE. This is a product property, not a deploy detail, and it is the thing that gets people. There is no password reset and no e-mail on the account, so a lost token is a lost portfolio unless they later add Google or OIDC sign-in. Make sure it is saved somewhere real before you close the session."
  - "DATABASE: Ghostfolio reads DATABASE_URL, so redu's injected value is the right shape, but build it explicitly from the injected parts so you control the query string. deploy_compose with database:'managed' APPENDS PGHOST, PGPORT, PGDATABASE, PGUSER, PGPASSWORD and DATABASE_URL to the project .env and never edits your compose, so your compose must interpolate: DATABASE_URL: \"postgresql://${PGUSER}:[REDACTED:conn-password]@${PGHOST}:${PGPORT}/${PGDATABASE}?connect_timeout=300\". ⚠️ Note the driver: apps/api/src/services/prisma/prisma.service.ts:12-22 uses @prisma/adapter-pg, i.e. node-postgres, NOT Prisma's Rust engine, so sslmode in the URL is interpreted by pg-connection-string, where require implies certificate verification and no-verify does not. That is the OPPOSITE of what sslmode=require means to the Go and libpq apps elsewhere in this library. Upstream's own example sets no sslmode at all; start there over redu's private network, and if you see a self-signed-certificate error, sslmode=no-verify is the node-postgres spelling of encrypt-but-do-not-verify. Say which you chose in the handover."
  - "THERE IS NO SQLITE FALLBACK, and that is worth knowing because most apps in this library have one. prisma/schema.prisma:7-9 declares postgresql and nothing else, and docker/entrypoint.sh runs under set -ex, so a wrong DATABASE_URL fails at prisma migrate deploy and the container exits. ⚠️ ONE CAVEAT: prisma.service.ts:44-50 CATCHES a connection failure at module init and only logs it, so the API process itself would happily listen against a dead database. PROVE THE WIRING IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. POSITIVE HALF, which also proves your command reached the app at all: GET /api/v1/health must return 200 with {\"status\":\"OK\"}, and health.service.ts:27-46 makes that a real Postgres query AND a real Redis ping, so one request covers both datastores. NEGATIVE HALF: sudo docker ps must show exactly TWO containers, ghostfolio and redis, i.e. you actually deleted the bundled postgres rather than quietly running two databases."
  - "⛔ DELETE THE postgres SERVICE AND ITS depends_on ENTRY. Upstream's compose ships postgres:15-alpine with a named volume. With database:'managed' redu provisions a Postgres on its own private VM, and if the compose still declares one you run both: the app talks to the managed one while a second database burns RAM on the app VM holding nothing. Removing a service without removing the depends_on block that names it makes compose refuse the file outright, which at least fails loudly."
  - "⛔ THE env_file LINES POINT OUTSIDE THE PROJECT AND WILL NOT RESOLVE. Every service in docker/docker-compose.yml declares env_file: ../.env, which is the repo root relative to the docker/ directory. You are uploading a tarball, not the repo, so that path does not exist and compose errors before anything starts. Drop the env_file lines and declare the variables in an environment: block instead: compose interpolates ${PGHOST} and friends from the project .env that deploy_compose writes, which is exactly what you want."
  - "KEEP REDIS IN THE COMPOSE, DELIBERATELY. Ghostfolio needs it for the Bull queues (market data gathering, portfolio snapshot computation), for the cache, and for the throttler counters once rate limiting is on. It is not a system of record: upstream's own compose gives it NO volume, so losing it on a redeploy costs a queue drain and a cold cache and no data. Keeping it in-compose also avoids a second managed datastore on the bill. Set REDIS_PASSWORD to a fresh value, and note the upstream redis command uses the shell-parameter form that FAILS to start if that variable is empty, which is a good failure."
  - "SET ROOT_URL TO THE FULL PUBLIC HTTPS URL, and generate the dname yourself in the complete `ghostfolio-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud` form so it is known at deploy time; a bare label gets a random suffix appended by redu and will not match. It defaults to http://0.0.0.0:3333 (apps/api/src/environments/environment.prod.ts), and it is what OAuth and OIDC callback URLs, the sitemap, the OpenGraph tags and the Ghostfolio data-provider URL are built from. The sharpest consequence: apps/api/src/app/auth/web-auth.service.ts:60-65 derives the WebAuthn relying-party id from new URL(ROOT_URL).hostname, so with the default left in place passkey registration fails with an origin mismatch that reads like a browser bug."
  - "PORT 3333, AND THERE IS NO LISTEN-ADDRESS TRAP HERE. libs/common/src/lib/config.ts:96,100 default HOST to 0.0.0.0 and PORT to 3333, and main.ts binds exactly those. Pass 3333 to deploy_compose. Every route is under /api/v1/ because main.ts:64-72 sets a global prefix of api and URI versioning defaulting to 1; the Angular frontend is served from the same port by the same process, so this stack has ONE ingress."
  - "WHAT AN ANONYMOUS REQUEST CAN REACH: the marketing and login pages of the frontend, GET /api/v1/health, GET /api/v1/info (which advertises which sign-in methods and whether signup is open), the sitemap, and any portfolio a user has explicitly shared through a public access link. POST /api/v1/user until you close it, and POST /api/v1/auth/anonymous, which is the token login. The Bull queue dashboard at /admin/queues is NOT open: apps/api/src/middlewares/bull-board-auth.middleware.ts requires a JWT with the admin permission and answers 403 otherwise."
  - "NO VOLUME IS NEEDED. Ghostfolio keeps activities, accounts, market data and settings in Postgres; the frontend assets are baked into the image; imports are parsed into the database rather than stored; and upstream gives Redis no volume on purpose. So the app VM is disposable and the managed database is the whole of your state. Do not add a volume and then believe it holds something."
  - "NO SUPERUSER AND NO SECOND DATABASE. prisma/migrations holds 119 migration files and the initial one contains no CREATE EXTENSION, CREATE SCHEMA or CREATE DATABASE; everything lives in one database as an ordinary role. Do NOT pass db_superuser:true. DIRECT_URL is optional and falls back to DATABASE_URL (.config/prisma.ts), so leave it unset: it exists for people behind a connection pooler, which redu is not."
  - "NO API KEY IS REQUIRED TO GET QUOTES, which surprises people who expect to shop for a market-data provider first. configuration.service.ts:62-64 defaults DATA_SOURCES to CoinGecko, MANUAL and Yahoo, and none of those needs a key. name: ghostfolio
services:
  ghostfolio:
    image: docker.io/ghostfolio/ghostfolio:latest
    container_name: ghostfolio
    restart: unless-stopped
    init: true
    cap_drop:
      - ALL
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true
    env_file:
      - ../.env
    ports:
      - 3333:3333
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD-SHELL', 'curl -f http://localhost:3333/api/v1/health']
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

  postgres:
    image: docker.io/library/postgres:15-alpine
    container_name: gf-postgres
    restart: unless-stopped
    cap_drop:
      - ALL
    cap_add:
      - CHOWN
      - DAC_READ_SEARCH
      - FOWNER
      - SETGID
      - SETUID
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true
    env_file:

      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
    volumes:

    container_name: gf-redis
    restart: unless-stopped
    user: '999:1000'
    cap_drop:
      - ALL
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true
    env_file:

Two steps, in this order: (1) POST /api/v1/user and check the response says role ADMIN, saving the accessToken it returns; (2) close signup with the next quirk. Never leave an unclaimed Ghostfolio on a public hostname."

YES, AND CLOSING IT IS A DATABASE ROW, NOT A SETTING YOU CAN SHIP. apps/api/src/services/property/property.service.ts:63-68 reads IS_USER_SIGNUP_ENABLED from the Property table and defaults to TRUE when the row is absent, and there is no environment variable that overrides it. ## Ghostfolio 3.53.0 is live

**https://ghostfolio-ywb2qlk3.redu.cloud**

### ⚠️ Save this now — it is shown once and cannot be reset

```
Security token:  «REDACTED:assigned:b5921016»
```

Ghostfolio's default sign-in has **no email and no password** — this token *is* your login, and this account is the administrator. There is no reset flow and no email on the account, so if you lose it the portfolio is unrecoverable (unless you later add Google or OIDC sign-in from inside the app). Put it in a password manager before you close this session.

Everything is also in `[REDACTED:value]` (mode 600), including **`ACCESS_TOKEN_SALT`** — that one must be passed *identically* on every redeploy. It's the salt your token is hashed under; change it and every account is locked out permanently, with all the data still sitting in Postgres and nothing erroring.

### The account was claimed before you got the URL

On a fresh Ghostfolio the first account created becomes admin, and account creation is anonymous and open — so that window was closed as part of the deploy, not left for you:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| App reachable, Postgres query + Redis ping | ✅ 200 `{"status":"OK"}` |
| Anonymous requests reach the API (positive control) | ✅ |
| Claimed account exists, token works, **is admin** | ✅ |
| Anonymous `POST /api/v1/user` refused | ✅ **403** |
| Frontend serves | ✅ 301 → `/en` → 200 |

`verify-ghostfolio.sh` exits 0. Rate limiting is genuinely enforcing, not just configured — repeated signup attempts went `403 403 403 429 429…`, so the throttler that normally skips itself is live.

### What's running

Exactly two containers, `ghostfolio` and `gf-redis`, both healthy with zero restarts — the bundled Postgres is gone, so you are not quietly running two databases. State lives entirely in the managed Postgres (db #163, private network only).

| | |
|---|---|
| App VM | m1.medium — £0.0278/hr |
| Managed Postgres | m1.small — £0.0174/hr |
| **Total** | **£0.0452/hr ≈ £33.00/mo** |

I deployed at m1.medium, not the m1.large `plan_deploy` quoted (£48.18/mo) — it upsizes compose stacks assuming an on-VM build, and nothing here is built. Measured idle usage says that was right: **347 MiB** for the app, 4 MiB for Redis, 1.0 GB of 3.9 GB host memory, zero OOM kills. Ready in 4m53s, with the 119 migrations taking 77s.

### Two answers your `redu.md` had flagged as open

- **No `sslmode` was needed** — a plain `?connect_timeout=300` over the private network connected first try, no certificate error.
- **Memory figure now recorded** (upstream publishes none).

### Files written

- `redu.md` — updated **surgically**: `last_deploy` recorded, the placeholder deploy-log line replaced with real measurements, and 6 new quirks appended. I deliberately hand-edited rather than letting the server rewrite the whole file, so your 24 accumulated quirks survive byte-for-byte; the only lines removed were the 4 placeholder ones. One new quirk is a trap I hit: once you drop `env_file`, Redis needs `REDIS_PASSWORD` in **its own** `environment` block, or its `:?` guard kills the container and it reads like a bad password rather than a missing one.
- `redu-deploy-plan.md` — real provisioned values, replacing the estimate.
- `deploy/docker-compose.yml`, `verify-ghostfolio.sh`, `[REDACTED:value]`.

### When you want it gone

`delete_deployment` removes the app VM **but deliberately keeps the Postgres**, which holds everything and keeps billing at £0.0174/hr. To stop paying entirely you also need `delete_database` on db #163.

One licence note: Ghostfolio is AGPL-3.0. Self-hosting the stock image for yourself is exactly the intended use and there's nothing to publish. Section 13 only bites if you *modify* it and let other people use it over a network — then those users are owed your modified source.
